title.en: Define population, sample, census and sample survey
Compare the census and sampling methods

say.en: To check whether rice is cooked, your mother tastes a few grains, not the whole pot. A doctor tests a few drops of blood, not all of it. That is sampling. In this lesson: Define population, sample, census and sample survey.
Compare the census and sampling methods.
Compute the sampling fraction.

body.en: The *population* (universe) is the whole group of units under study, e.g. all households of a town. It may be finite or infinite. The census method studies every unit of the population (complete enumeration). A sample is a part of the population selected to represent it, and a sample survey studies only the sample and draws conclusions about the population. Sampling fraction = n/N.
body.kn: ಸಮಷ್ಟಿ (ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ) ಎಂದರೆ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಘಟಕಗಳ ಸಮೂಹ. ಜನಗಣತಿ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಘಟಕವನ್ನು ಅಧ್ಯಯನಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಮಾದರಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಸಮಷ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರತಿನಿಧಿಸುವ ಭಾಗ; ಮಾದರಿ ಸಮೀಕ್ಷೆ ಅದರ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ಸಮಷ್ಟಿಯ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ನಿರ್ಣಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

text.en: Counting every person in India for the national Census
Report cards with the marks of all 40 students of a class

Testing how long the bulbs from a factory last
Tasting a spoon of sambar to check the salt
Estimating the yield of rice in Karnataka by crop-cutting
Checking a lot of crackers for safety

explanation.en: Use a census when the population is small or every unit must be counted (national census, a class register). Use a sample when testing destroys the unit (bulbs, blood, crackers, tasting food) or the population is very large.

say.en: Which method suits each enquiry: a census every unit or a sample survey?
say.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿಚಾರಣೆಗೆ ಯಾವುದು ಸೂಕ್ತ: ಗಣತಿ (ಪ್ರತಿ ಘಟಕ) ಅಥವಾ ಮಾದರಿ ಸಮೀಕ್ಷೆ?

body.en: *Census*: data on every unit, more accurate and reliable, suitable when the population is small or very varied, and needed for national counts like the Census of India (every 10 years). But it is costly, slow and needs many workers. Sampling: saves time, money and labour, allows trained staff and deeper study, and is the only way when testing destroys units (bulbs, blood, crackers) or the population is infinite. But it has sampling error and needs expert planning to avoid bias.
body.kn: ಜನಗಣತಿ: ಪ್ರತಿ ಘಟಕದ ಮಾಹಿತಿ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನಿಖರ; ಆದರೆ ದುಬಾರಿ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಧಾನ. ಮಾದರಿ: ಸಮಯ, ಹಣ, ಶ್ರಮ ಉಳಿತಾಯ; ನಾಶಕಾರಿ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಅಥವಾ ಅನಂತ ಸಮಷ್ಟಿಗೆ ಏಕೈಕ ಮಾರ್ಗ; ಆದರೆ ಮಾದರಿ ದೋಷ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A factory makes 10,000 bulbs a day. To test their life it tests 100 bulbs, costing ₹20 per test. Why sample? Find the sampling fraction and the testing cost of a census and of the sample.

steps.en: Testing life burns the bulb out: a census would destroy all 10,000 bulbs. So sampling is the only way.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A factory makes 10,000 bulbs a day. To test their life it tests 100 bulbs, costing ₹20 per test. Why sample? Find the sampling fraction and the testing cost of a census and of the sample.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A factory makes 10,000 bulbs a day. To test their life it tests 100 bulbs, costing 20 rupees per test. Why sample? Find the sampling fraction and the testing cost of a census and of the sample.
Testing life burns the bulb out: a census would destroy all 10,000 bulbs. So sampling is the only way.
Sampling fraction equals 100 divided by 10,000 equals 0.01 equals 1 percent.
Census cost equals 10,000 times 20 rupees equals 2,00,000 rupees; sample cost equals 100 times 20 rupees equals 2,000 rupees.
So the answer is Sampling is necessary; fraction 1 percent; 2,00,000 rupees vs 2,000 rupees.
